doc.title: Frank Foster and Bill Hughes interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Schenectady, New York, March 28, 1995

chapter: Jazz today and writing for Joe Williams
title: Head tunes: Every Day and the M Squad theme
summary: Hughes and Foster recall tunes built from heads, including Thad Jones shaping the M Squad theme.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: we used to say a lot of the licks that Ernie put into “Every Day” we’d already like set those things, and he wrote them in.

Right. And then there were two songs that were heads from “Jump City”: “I Got a Gal”— “Roll ‘Em Pete” and “Shake, Rattle and Roll.” Not a note of music written for either of those full fledged arrangements. I mean the audience would never know the difference. That was going back to the old days in the best way possible — totally from the head. Then there was recording that we did, now this was, this was off the subject of Joe Williams, remember when they had the M Squad, that detective story on television? They wanted a theme for the M Squad and they came to me unfortunately, and they brought me a sketch of somebody from the studio had written this dumb sketch, and I was supposed to make something up. And it wasn’t a blues, it was just like eight bars of some nonsense, and I said now what am I going to do with this? And I labored over this mess, and I tried to make something out of it and I just, man I’m just not one for taking ideas of others and turning them into something, especially when they, I can’t use the word—

So we got in the studio and they ran it down and it’s, “well, I don’t know, we’re looking for something” — So Thad Jones, Frank Wess and I put our heads together and Thad did most of the work, it was “you play this note, you play this, and let’s take this little riff and you play this.” And he came out with the M Squad theme with not a note of music written, totally a head tune. [scats] Well that’s what it was, that’s how it started out.
You know what’s a direct rip off on that?
“Thirty-three and a Third Detective” a direct rip off.
Naked Gun, yeah right, what’s his name?
I don’t know who did the arrangement on the thing.
